hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5712.context: Other humans show mercy to gods, but they do not give what they ask for, even when ignorant.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5713.meaning: True contentment comes from using material things wisely, not from excess or greed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_5713.context: No wealth, clothes, pleasures, gold, cows, or food can distort one if used properly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6036.meaning: When we let go of distractions, we can fully concentrate and achieve our goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6036.context: Kasyapa sees earth giving blessings, enters earth of others, frees himself, focuses on task.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6037.meaning: True strength comes from staying calm and trusting that good will prevail.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6037.context: She is covered with grass, herbs; king sits calmly, not fearing loss of righteousness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6038.meaning: Long-term commitment and steady effort lead to lasting success and inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6038.context: He keeps vows for many divine years; for thirty years Kasyapa stays grounded, no laziness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6039.meaning: Respecting wise teachers honors the lineage and brings blessings to all.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6039.context: Great king arrives, bows to Kasyapa; Prithivi Kasyapa is born to a great sage.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6040.meaning: Recognizing true qualities matters more than titles or social status.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6040.context: King says Kasyapa is not a Brahmin; asks for another, best Kshatriya.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6041.meaning: Heed wise counsel and listen to those with experience for guidance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6041.context: King is silent; wind speaks again, telling him to listen to Uthathya from Angirasa family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6042.meaning: Mutual respect and equality strengthen relationships and bring harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6042.context: Bhadra, daughter of Soma, is seen as supreme; she sees her husband, equal to her.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6043.meaning: Hard work and devotion can protect and uplift those around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_13_6043.context: Lady performs intense austerities; he covers Utathya, who is very fortunate.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_114.meaning: Listening to wise advice can remove jealousy from your heart and bring peace to your soul.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_114.context: Indra felt jealous until Brihaspati spoke wise words to calm his angry heart and mind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_115.meaning: Ancient stories teach us valuable lessons about how people should treat each other with respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_115.context: The speaker shares an old story about a talk between the priest Brihaspati and King Marutta.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_116.meaning: Anger often comes when we feel rejected or overlooked by those we respect deeply.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_116.context: King Marutta got very angry when he heard that the priest had chosen another king instead.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_117.meaning: Taking bold action and speaking up can help you achieve your important spiritual goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_117.context: The king decided to perform a big ritual and went to speak with the god Indra.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_118.meaning: Keeping your promises and honoring past agreements builds trust and respect between people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_118.context: The king reminded the god of their past agreement and promised to follow his instructions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_119.meaning: True devotion means offering your whole self and asking for guidance from those who know.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_119.context: The king offered himself and his preparations to the priest, asking for guidance on the ritual.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_137.meaning: Avoiding a difficult person or problem can lead to serious trouble and destruction later.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_137.context: The speaker warns the king to go to the woman and not ignore the situation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_138.meaning: When you face darkness or fear, seeking help from God brings safety and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_138.context: The man followed the powerful figure into the dark and prayed to God with folded hands.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_328.meaning: True spirit cannot be harmed by physical attacks. It remains strong and alive no matter what happens to the body.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_328.context: Krishna explains his divine nature to Arjuna, stating that no weapon or force can truly destroy his eternal self.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_329.meaning: You cannot destroy truth with actions or money. The real self always returns and stays present in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_329.context: The speaker says that even if people try to end him through rituals or gifts, he will simply appear again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_330.meaning: Intellectual arguments cannot kill the soul. Peace and truth exist beyond words and stay calm forever.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_330.context: Even using sacred texts or deep philosophy to try and defeat him fails, as he remains calm and beyond reach.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_331.meaning: Trying to fight truth makes you part of it. You do not see how it changes your feelings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_331.context: Those who patiently try to destroy him are brave, but they fail to understand that he becomes their own emotion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_332.meaning: Life is eternal and joyful. You cannot escape it, so accept that you are part of this endless whole.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_332.context: The wise seek freedom but cannot kill the eternal one, who laughs and remains the name of all beings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_334.meaning: Do your duty and help others. Good actions bring peace and keep your life balanced and right.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_334.context: The speaker advises the king to perform duties and give gifts to fulfill desires and maintain righteousness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_335.meaning: Generosity and following traditions show respect. Giving freely helps you connect with higher values and community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_335.context: Performing grand rituals like horse sacrifices and giving many gifts is described as a way to honor the divine.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_336.meaning: Devotion and generosity lead to honor. Doing good things brings respect and guides you to a better life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_336.context: By worshipping with great sacrifices and rich gifts, one attains high fame and the best spiritual path.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_415.meaning: Listen carefully to understand the deepest truth. Seeing perfection helps you learn the most important spiritual lessons in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_415.context: A wise teacher speaks to his student about seeing the highest truth and perfection in the world.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_416.meaning: Your good deeds and spiritual focus determine your future. Act well now to reach a better place later.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_416.context: The teacher explains that your actions and spiritual practices decide where you go after you die.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_417.meaning: Bad desires lead to pain. Recognizing your past mistakes helps you avoid repeating them and find peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_417.context: The speaker admits to past bad choices driven by anger, lust, and selfish desires that caused suffering.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_419.meaning: Life repeats in many forms. Understanding this cycle helps you see beyond temporary physical needs and pleasures.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_419.context: The soul experiences many lives, eating and drinking different foods while going through cycles of birth and death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_420.meaning: Relationships change over time. Accept that joy and pain are temporary parts of the human journey.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_420.context: The speaker recalls having many different parents and experiencing both great joy and deep sorrow across lives.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_421.meaning: Wealth and friends come and go. Do not attach your happiness to things that can easily disappear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_421.context: The speaker describes living with friends and enemies, losing wealth, and gaining it with great sadness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_422.meaning: Life brings hard times. Endure pain with strength and do not let shame define your true self.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_422.context: The speaker mentions facing shame, suffering from family issues, and enduring terrible physical and mental pain.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_423.meaning: Violence leads to deep suffering. Choose peace and kindness to avoid the pain that comes from harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_423.context: The speaker describes the destruction of armies and the terrible suffering that leads to hellish states.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_518.meaning: True wisdom means seeing the divine spirit inside everything around you instead of just looking at the outside world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_518.context: The speaker introduces a deep teaching about yoga and how wise people see the true self everywhere.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_519.meaning: You must look inside your own heart and mind to discover who you really are deep down.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_519.context: A student asks the teacher to explain how a wise person finds their true self within their own mind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_520.meaning: When you stop being proud and selfish, you can finally see your true nature without any confusion or noise.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_520.context: A wise person removes pride and ego from their heart to see their true self clearly with their mind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_522.meaning: Solitude helps you connect with your inner self because you are not distracted by other people or things.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_522.context: The wise person sits alone in silence and focuses their attention inward to find their true self within.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_523.meaning: When you control your own desires and emotions, you can understand and see other people much better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_523.context: By controlling the senses and staying steady, a person masters themselves and then sees others with clear eyes.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_524.meaning: Realize that you are deeply connected to everyone else, just as everything in a dream is part of your mind.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_524.context: Just like a dreamer sees things in a dream, the wise person sees their self connected to all others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_525.meaning: You must strip away outer distractions to reveal the pure spirit that lives inside your physical body.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_525.context: Like removing a cover to reveal an arrow, the yogi removes distractions to see the true self inside the body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_526.meaning: Your physical body is just a temporary container, so focus on returning to your eternal spiritual nature.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_526.context: The body is like a small seed or shell, and the wise person wants to merge back into their true self.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1062.meaning: Understanding the world requires using all senses, and each sense helps us learn different aspects of reality.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1062.context: A guide explains how five beings use four senses to learn about the world.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1063.meaning: True spirituality involves recognizing the divine in everyday actions, especially those that guide us toward higher truths.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1063.context: Sages say feet are spiritual, but reaching the divine is about Vishnu and higher powers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1064.meaning: Our inner spirit connects us to higher beings, reminding us that we are part of a larger divine plan.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1064.context: The present spirit is called Adhyatma, and it talks about gods and the supreme lord.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1066.meaning: Using our hands for good reflects our spiritual nature and honors the divine actions that inspire us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1066.context: Spiritual people see hands as sacred, and they praise Indra for his divine deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1067.meaning: Spiritual thought fuels inner fire, helping us connect with divine energy and grow stronger inside.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1067.context: The mind of Vaishvadevi is called spiritual, and it speaks about fire and divine power.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1068.meaning: Seeing the moon as divine reminds us that nature reflects higher truths and guides our spiritual journey.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1068.context: Spiritual minds follow five beings, and the moon is seen as a divine symbol.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1069.meaning: Our thinking connects us to the divine, showing that intellect can lead us to higher spiritual understanding.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1069.context: The intellect is spiritual, and it thinks about six senses, while Brahma is the ultimate source.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1070.meaning: Meditating on senses and divine beings helps unify mind and spirit, leading to deeper inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1070.context: All senses, objects, and five great beings should be combined for meditation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1174.meaning: Doing your duty with a pure heart is important. Acceptance comes from inner purity and right action.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1174.context: Brahmins have many duties like teaching and sacrifice. Pure people are accepted in these roles.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1176.meaning: Giving to others and learning are good deeds. They make your life right and help you grow.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1176.context: Charity, study, and sacrifice are listed as righteous actions. These deeds help a person grow spiritually.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1178.meaning: Self control and doing your best leads to success. You will find peace and happiness in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1178.context: A householder who controls himself and does his duties well will succeed. He gains spiritual rewards.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1179.meaning: Focus on your studies and keep your life simple. Dedication helps you reach your highest goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1179.context: He studied hard and lived a celibate life. This shows dedication to learning and spiritual growth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1180.meaning: Accept what you receive with a thankful heart. Do not complain about simple food or conditions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1180.context: With teacher permission, he ate food without complaint. He accepted what he got with gratitude.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1182.meaning: Stay calm during rituals and daily tasks. Carry your responsibilities with peace and steady focus.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1182.context: He offered sacrifices to fire while staying calm. He carried a staff as a sign of his path.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1183.meaning: What you wear does not define you. Focus on your inner character rather than outer appearance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1183.context: Clothes could be silk, cotton, or skin. The material did not matter as much as the intent.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1184.meaning: Keep a regular routine for your body and mind. Discipline in small habits builds strong character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1184.context: He wore a belt and had matted hair. He followed daily routines like bathing and studying.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1185.meaning: Focus your mind on spiritual growth and detach from worldly status to find true inner freedom and peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1185.context: A wise person focuses on higher goals and stays away from social groups to find peace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1187.meaning: Leaving behind busy social life helps you find silence and focus on your spiritual path and growth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1187.context: A holy man leaves his home and village to live alone in the quiet forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1188.meaning: Commit fully to your chosen path of simplicity and do not let old habits pull you back.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1188.context: The wanderer wears simple clothes and stays in the forest without returning to village life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1189.meaning: Showing hospitality to strangers is a sacred duty that builds community and reflects your inner kindness and generosity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1189.context: You must welcome guests with kindness and provide them with food and a safe place to rest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1190.meaning: Live simply by taking only what nature provides and maintain a disciplined routine in your daily life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1190.context: The seeker gathers natural food from the forest and eats it with discipline and without laziness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1191.meaning: Generosity is a key virtue, so always share your resources with those in need without feeling reluctant.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1191.context: If you have extra food, you should share it with others generously and without any hesitation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1192.meaning: Practice self-control in eating and speaking to maintain a light heart and connect with spiritual peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1192.context: Eat with moderation and keep your speech calm to stay healthy and find refuge in the divine.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1193.meaning: True wisdom comes from being honest, forgiving, and kind to others while living a life of integrity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1193.context: Be kind, forgiving, and truthful while maintaining a simple appearance and dedicating yourself to right actions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1754.meaning: Even powerful beings can change, and we should not worry about their past mistakes or future actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1754.context: The gods travel to endless worlds, conquering themselves, and the speaker says no one should regret this.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1756.meaning: True wisdom comes from a pure heart, growing steadily like a bright moon in a calm sky.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1756.context: A great soul’s father, who knows right, grew like a moon inside a white winged womb.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1757.meaning: Sometimes leaders must leave after fulfilling their duties, showing humility and acceptance of change.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1757.context: An old man woke the righteous king, who then vanished after the Ashwamedha ceremony.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1758.meaning: Listening to wise counsel helps a ruler think clearly and make good decisions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1758.context: The wise king listened to Vyas, whose words reached his mind like a spinning wheel.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1759.meaning: A king’s actions are guided by wise advice, showing respect for tradition and responsibility.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1759.context: After hearing Brahmin Vyasena, the king prepared to perform the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1760.meaning: Even small objects can hold deep meaning, prompting us to seek truth beyond appearances.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1760.context: A gem placed by Marut on the ground sparked a question about its true nature.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1761.meaning: Unity and communication among family strengthen leadership and help face challenges together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1761.context: Yudhisthira heard Davaipayana, gathered his brothers, and spoke to Arjuna, Bhimasena, and Yama.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1762.meaning: Hard work, friendship, and teaching good values build a strong, moral character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_1762.context: He grew through hard work, caring for friends, and teaching righteous deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2211.meaning: This moment shows how divine beings interact with humans. It highlights the connection between gods and mortal lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2211.context: The goddess wakes up and sees Ulupi. She speaks to the serpent daughter about the recent events.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2212.meaning: A mother will do anything for her child. Her love drives her actions even in tragic times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2212.context: Ulupi looks at her dead husband. She tells the goddess she won the contest for her child.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2213.meaning: True virtue is recognized even in sorrow. A chaste woman is honored for her deep devotion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2213.context: The goddess praises Ulupi for her virtue. She notes the husband died because of her sake.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2214.meaning: Grief can make us feel guilty. We often seek forgiveness when we lose someone we love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2214.context: Ulupi blames herself for the death. She begs Arjuna to forgive her and bring him back.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2215.meaning: Wisdom helps us accept fate. A wise person understands that some things are beyond control.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2215.context: The goddess praises Ulupi again. She is amazed that Ulupi does not regret the deaths.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2216.meaning: We value different relationships in unique ways. Duty and love create complex feelings of regret.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2216.context: Ulupi says she does not regret her son. She only regrets her husband and his hospitality.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2217.meaning: Life continues even after loss. New beginnings often follow the end of a difficult chapter.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2217.context: Ulupi gives birth to a goddess. She says she will now go back to her husband.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2218.meaning: Fulfilling promises is important. Keeping your word shows respect and honor to those you love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2218.context: Ulupi calls to her husband. She says she has delivered the horse to him safely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2299.meaning: He shows respect and warns that he will not fight or disturb the king’s peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2299.context: A warrior speaks to a powerful king, saying he will not enter the city.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2301.meaning: The journey shows that even a simple animal can guide people to important places.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2301.context: A horse travels across the sea, then turns toward the royal city of Nagahvaya.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2304.meaning: Unexpected paths can lead to new opportunities and adventures.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2304.context: A crowned hero follows the horse and arrives by chance at Rajagriha city.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2305.meaning: Good people stand up against evil, even when the world seems bleak.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2305.context: The king, grandson of Jarasandha, faces darkness while a righteous hero calls for battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2306.meaning: Even great warriors can be confused by hidden truths that others see.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2306.context: Arjuna reaches a clouded meeting place, but the young king does not understand it.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2307.meaning: The speaker wants to protect or control something that is being misused.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2307.context: A horse is compared to a woman, and the speaker wants to take it away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2308.meaning: He shows confidence that his actions will end the conflict and bring peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2308.context: Pandava laughs at others and says he has done his best to stop the troublemaker.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2311.meaning: He encourages fair competition and calmness while overcoming rivals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_14_2311.context: The king says his eldest brother knows this, urging to defeat others without anger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_541.meaning: It shows the farmer’s curiosity and the Lord’s willingness to explain His true form and purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_541.context: A farmer asks the Lord to reveal His nature and why he is being asked.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_542.meaning: It teaches that sincere listening and sharing wisdom help keep young hearts pure and strong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_542.context: Narada speaks with full devotion, and a wise ascetic listens, sharing his youthful energy with good people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_543.meaning: It reminds us that even gods interact with kings, showing that everyone can learn from divine examples.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_543.context: Indra visits his wife Sachi and speaks to the king, sharing a chance encounter with royalty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_544.meaning: It shows that great effort in spiritual work can be hard but is worth listening to and learning from.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_544.context: The king hears a story about Dhritarashtra and his difficult spiritual practices, told by Indra.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_545.meaning: It suggests that a long life can bring wisdom and the chance to do good deeds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_545.context: The king lives many years, experiencing a long and stable life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_546.meaning: It teaches that true devotion and good actions can cleanse one’s past mistakes and bring honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_546.context: A son of a sage rides a flying chariot, wearing divine jewelry, and his sins are burned by his practices.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_548.meaning: It shows that recognizing and sharing a person’s good qualities encourages others to follow them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_548.context: The speaker tells the Lord about a great secret, praising his wealth of virtues and his cleansed sins.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_550.meaning: It illustrates how kindness and beauty can attract positive attention and honor from others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_550.context: The divine sage speaks sweet words, and the king surrounds himself with flowers as a sign of respect.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_848.meaning: Leaders should look dignified and ready to act with honor and strength.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_848.context: Kings gather in a grand hall wearing bright clothes and holding their weapons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_850.meaning: True power comes from staying calm and free from anger or pride.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_850.context: The assembled kings wear beautiful clothes and heavy jewelry while staying calm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_851.meaning: Beauty and joy can lift the spirit and create a peaceful atmosphere.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_851.context: Celestial singers perform while a queen in fine robes is surrounded by fairies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_852.meaning: Deep focus and faith can unlock hidden abilities and change your reality.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_852.context: King Dhritarashtra, who is blind, gains special sight through deep spiritual practice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_853.meaning: Love and spiritual strength can help us see the truth beyond physical limits.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_853.context: Queen Gandhari uses her divine power to see all her sons who died in war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_854.meaning: Sometimes the truth is so shocking that it changes how we see the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_854.context: Everyone is shocked and amazed to see the dead sons appear before them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_855.meaning: Sharing happiness with others can make life feel light and wonderful.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_855.context: The kings enjoy a night of pure joy, feeling as if they are in heaven.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_856.meaning: Wisdom and grace can heal old wounds and turn enemies into friends.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_856.context: The sage's blessing helps the kings drop their anger and become friends.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_904.meaning: Hard work and discipline help you grow wise. You should seek out people who know more than you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_904.context: Vidura used hard work to gain wisdom. Dhritarashtra then went to meet a holy man.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_905.meaning: We often see our parents in others. This shows how deep our love and respect for them truly is.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_905.context: The king speaks to a sage. He sees the sage as a reflection of his own father.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_906.meaning: Sometimes we must wait for the right time. Trust that your deep wishes will be met in due course.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_906.context: The king wants to stay with the sage. He hopes his wish to have a child comes true.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_907.meaning: Realizing how short life is can change you. It helps you let go of pride and fear.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_907.context: The king feels very old after hearing these words. He is moved by the deep spiritual truth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_908.meaning: Good times do come after hard ones. Seeing loved ones happy brings us great peace and joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_908.context: A beautiful time arrives for the king. Janamejaya sees his father looking very happy and healthy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_909.meaning: We are all connected to others. Seeing the people around us reminds us of our shared human bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_909.context: The king sees his father and the sage. He also sees the ministers who serve the royal family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_910.meaning: Family time is precious. Being together with loved ones brings true happiness and a sense of belonging.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_910.context: Janamejaya is very happy to see his father. He sits down with his father and his wife.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_911.meaning: New life brings hope and continuity. Every person has a role to play in the story of the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_911.context: The king bathes and speaks to Astika. A son named Jaratkaru is born to the sage's family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1033.meaning: Even the strongest heroes can fail when facing overwhelming odds, showing that courage does not guarantee victory.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1033.context: Older relatives watched sadly as the brave son of Madravati failed to save his family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1034.meaning: Sharing pain with loved ones helps us cope, and true friendship means standing together in hard times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1034.context: The five brothers held each other tightly while crying because they were deeply hurt and scared.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1035.meaning: Wisdom and spiritual power can guide us through difficult paths, and rituals help connect us to the divine.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1035.context: A wise man who ate wind went into the woods to start a holy fire ritual.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1038.meaning: True inner light shines brighter than physical fire, and spiritual growth illuminates the world around you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1038.context: As the man grew older, the forest had no fire, but ascetics said it was lit by his spirit.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1039.meaning: Truth is revealed through careful observation and honest reporting, helping leaders understand the current situation clearly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1039.context: The speaker told Yudhisthira that King Jahnavi was in Kachcha and had joined with a specific body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1041.meaning: Honesty about our mistakes and fears is important, and acknowledging truth helps us move forward with clarity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1041.context: The speaker admitted to seeing demon sages on the river bank and confessed his own sinful actions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1042.meaning: Death is a transition to a higher state, and we should not worry too much about those who have passed on.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1042.context: The wise man told the king he was united with fire and had reached his final destination.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1043.meaning: Dedicated service to a wise guide leads to spiritual growth, and honoring teachers brings great inner peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_15_1043.context: Arjuna was told that his mother achieved great perfection through her service to her spiritual teacher.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_225.meaning: We can change our future; destiny is not fixed, and we must act with hope.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_225.context: Arjuna feels worried, thinking fate is fixed, but Rajan reminds him nothing is set in stone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_226.meaning: Sharing wisdom and gifts can influence events, but also bring challenges to those involved.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_226.context: A woman gives her great mind to someone, and a precious gem falls to the battlefield.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_227.meaning: Powerful actions can separate allies and enemies, showing how decisions affect many lives.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_227.context: He brings his wife and takes the rest of the Vrishnis, sending Arjuna and the Kauravas away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_228.meaning: Even great people can make mistakes, and their choices can hurt others in unexpected ways.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_228.context: A son of Partha visits Martikavatam, where the best men took the king of Bhoja’s wife.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_229.meaning: Dividing resources and moving people can change relationships and create new paths.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_229.context: The Pandavas split the old and young parts, and Indra sends them across the river.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_230.meaning: Good deeds and kindness are honored, and children grow up with positive influences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_230.context: Yuyudhani is born to Saraswati, son of Satyakina, and a righteous woman rewards the child.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_232.meaning: Many people come together, showing unity and shared purpose in a larger community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_16_232.context: Rukmini, Gandhari, Shaibya, Haimavati, and Jambavati join the Jataveda group.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_177.meaning: Nature provides plenty of resources, so we should be grateful for the earth's gifts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_177.context: The land is described as having many large ponds that are full of water.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_178.meaning: Sharing positive news makes the world a happier and more joyful place for everyone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_178.context: A wise person tells a young child that good news has been shared widely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_180.meaning: When people work together with good intentions, the whole community becomes stronger and better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_180.context: The king is told that his subjects are working hard and doing good deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_181.meaning: We must stay alert and protect our community from those who wish to cause harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_181.context: The king is warned that thieves and bad people are moving around the land.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_183.meaning: Trust and discretion are important, and keeping promises helps maintain peace and safety.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_183.context: The king is told that his people are safe and keeping their secrets well.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_184.meaning: Reflecting on our past helps us understand ourselves better and learn from our history.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_184.context: A wise man listens at night and thinks deeply about his past experiences.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_185.meaning: Even in rest, we should keep our minds focused on doing what is right and good.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_185.context: The king thinks about duty and wealth while resting during the night hours.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_186.meaning: Leaders should be punctual and prepared, showing respect for their duties and their people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_186.context: The wise king wakes up at the right time with his advisors ready to work.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_534.meaning: Running away from danger is wise when you are weak. Protecting your life allows you to fight another day.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_534.context: The speaker recalls fearing the powerful enemy Jarasandha. They fled their home city of Mathura to find safety in Dwaravati.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_535.meaning: You must remove the main obstacle to achieve your goal. Taking bold action can save many lives and honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_535.context: The speaker urges the king to act. He suggests killing Jarasandha to save the people and complete the sacred ritual.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_536.meaning: You cannot finish a big task if a major problem blocks you. Solve the main issue before proceeding further.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_536.context: The speaker admits the task is hard. He asks how he can fully perform the royal sacrifice without removing the threat first.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_537.meaning: Share your thoughts openly and listen to others. Make decisions with clear reasons so everyone understands the path forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_537.context: The speaker offers his honest opinion to the king. He asks the king to decide wisely and explain his final choice clearly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_538.meaning: True wisdom stands out clearly to others. When you speak with certainty and truth, people recognize your value and respect you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_538.context: The king praises the speaker for his wise words. He agrees that no one else on earth could speak with such clarity.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_539.meaning: Power comes in different forms and levels. Being strong does not mean you control everything. Know your true place in the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_539.context: The text discusses the role of kings. It notes that while kings are powerful, they do not always hold the full title of emperor.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_540.meaning: Do not praise everyone just to be nice. Real respect grows when people work together and support each other with honest hearts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_540.context: The speaker questions how one can praise everyone. He notes that true praise comes when people unite and respect each other genuinely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_541.meaning: Great resources require great knowledge to manage. Leaders must understand their territory deeply to guide their people effectively and safely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_541.context: The land is described as vast and rich with gems. The leader of the clan travels far and knows the land well.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1544.meaning: Seeking wisdom from those who know the truth helps us understand our past and find peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1544.context: The king asks for advice and the wise man shares his deep knowledge of ancient texts.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1545.meaning: Listening with an open heart allows us to learn valuable lessons from the stories of others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1545.context: The speaker invites the king to listen carefully to a detailed story about important events.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1546.meaning: Even when we hear good advice, we may still struggle with our own stubborn thoughts and feelings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1546.context: After hearing wise counsel, the king and his son speak again in a lonely place.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1547.meaning: True wisdom earns respect from others and protects us from the harm of gossip.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1547.context: People in the land respect Vidura and no wise person would speak badly about him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1548.meaning: Following the guidance of wise mentors leads to the best outcomes for our lives and families.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1548.context: The father believes that listening to Vidura is the best choice for his son's future.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1549.meaning: Ancient wisdom from respected teachers reminds us that truth and righteousness are always the right path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1549.context: The speaker quotes a wise teacher of gods to support the importance of listening to truth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1550.meaning: Trusting those who see the full picture helps us navigate life with confidence and clarity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1550.context: Vidura knows all the hidden truths and the speaker trusts his words completely and deeply.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1551.meaning: Intelligence and good character make a person worthy of honor and respect from their community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1551.context: Vidura is seen as the smartest man among the clan and is honored by many leaders.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1790.meaning: Pride in victory can blind us to the true cost of conflict and the suffering it causes others around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1790.context: A speaker boasts about winning a great prize from a rival during a tense and dramatic moment in the story.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1791.meaning: Material riches are temporary and cannot buy true happiness or peace, so do not place your trust in money alone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1791.context: The speaker describes a massive treasure of gold coins and pots, claiming this vast wealth belongs to the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1792.meaning: Listen carefully before you speak, as your response shapes the outcome of the situation and reveals your true character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1792.context: Shakuni responds to the king after hearing the previous claims, preparing to make his own move in the game.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1793.meaning: True strength often moves with quiet grace and dignity, showing that power does not need to be loud or aggressive.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1793.context: A royal chariot is described as the finest vehicle, moving silently like clouds over a calm and holy ocean.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1795.meaning: Use your natural talents and strengths to serve others with excellence, rather than using them for selfish gain or pride.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1795.context: Eight fine horses are praised for their speed and grace, lifting their feet high as they carry the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1796.meaning: Dishonesty may bring short term wins, but it destroys trust and leads to long term failure and deep regret for all.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1796.context: Shakuni uses trickery and deception against the young king, trying to win the game through dishonest and unfair means.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1797.meaning: Great power requires great responsibility, and using strength to protect others is far nobler than using it for war.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1797.context: Powerful elephants with huge teeth are described as fierce warriors capable of carrying kings and fighting in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1799.meaning: External displays of power and wealth are fleeting, so focus on building inner character and kindness instead of status.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1799.context: The elephants are compared to heavy mountain clouds breaking through the city, showcasing the king's immense and mighty wealth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1871.meaning: He shows he is willing to lose everything he owns to keep his word and honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1871.context: Yudhisthira lists his animals and land as his total wealth during the gambling match.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1872.meaning: Clever people often use lies to trap others into making bad choices for their own gain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1872.context: Shakuni uses a trick to make Yudhisthira bet more than he can afford to lose.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1873.meaning: His desperation shows how dangerous it is to risk everything you care about in a gamble.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1873.context: Yudhisthira offers the whole kingdom and its people as his next stake in the game.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1874.meaning: When someone keeps pushing you to bet more, it is a sign they are trying to cheat you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1874.context: Shakuni continues his deceptive tactics to push Yudhisthira into betting his own freedom.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1875.meaning: He is giving up his personal identity and status to try to win back what he lost.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1875.context: Yudhisthira takes off his jewelry and offers it as part of his stake in the match.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1876.meaning: Greed and deception can lead a person to sacrifice the people they love most for a game.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1876.context: Shakuni keeps using his wits to trick Yudhisthira into betting his brothers next.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1878.meaning: They realize the trap is closing in and question the fairness of the current situation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1878.context: The brothers ask how Yudhisthira can bet them since they are already his property.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1879.meaning: Sometimes the most powerful move is to stay silent and let the other person face the consequences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_1879.context: Shakuni turns away after making his point, leaving the brothers in a difficult position.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2025.meaning: Spreading lies brings bad karma. You will face the full punishment for your dishonest actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2025.context: This verse warns people against spreading false stories or lies in public gatherings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2026.meaning: Old stories hold deep wisdom. Listening to them helps us learn from the past.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2026.context: The speaker mentions an old story told by a sage to a young boy named Parahlada.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2027.meaning: Power does not excuse bad behavior. Even kings must respect truth and righteousness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2027.context: A demon king and his son are involved in a conflict with holy sages.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2028.meaning: Desires can be strong, but we should seek divine guidance for our wishes.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2028.context: A character named Jayayan speaks about wanting a daughter and mentions a divine presence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2029.meaning: Secrets and arguments can cause division. It is better to speak openly and honestly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2029.context: People are arguing about a question and asking others to keep it secret.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2030.meaning: Anger burns us from the inside. We should stay calm and not let rage control us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2030.context: Sudhanva looks at another person with anger, feeling like a burning staff.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2031.meaning: Lies have serious consequences. Honesty protects you from self-destruction and bad luck.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2031.context: A severe warning is given that lying will cause great physical and spiritual harm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2032.meaning: Actions have reactions. When things go wrong, seek wise advice to find a solution.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_2_2032.context: Sudhanva is struck by a weapon, and a demon goes to a sage for help.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_248.meaning: They decide to use force to stop the Pandavas, showing their aggressive plan.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_248.context: The Kauravas prepare weapons, chariots, and plan to hunt the Pandavas in the forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_249.meaning: They show devotion and agree to follow the plan, trusting their leader.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_249.context: After hearing a message, the warriors worship again and answer Sutaja affirmatively.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_252.meaning: Their anger drives them to split up and attack, showing divided intent.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_252.context: The warriors leave in anger, each group determined to kill the Pandavas.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_253.meaning: Krishna uses his clear vision to confront the opposing side with calm purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_253.context: Krishna, pure and wise, sees the Kauravas as enemies and approaches them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_254.meaning: The Lord’s authority is respected, and the wise man seeks guidance with open eyes.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_254.context: The Lord, revered worldwide, commands everyone, and a wise man quickly approaches the seated figure.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_255.meaning: He offers guidance to help his people, showing concern for their well-being.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_255.context: Dhritarashtra speaks, promising to give wise advice for the Kauravas’ welfare.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_256.meaning: He shifts responsibility, showing how leaders avoid accountability.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_257.meaning: He warns that anger can lead to destructive actions and warns against rash decisions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_269.meaning: Love for family can make us hesitate to do hard things even when duty calls.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_270.meaning: Having a good child is the greatest blessing a parent can receive in this life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_271.meaning: Money and power cannot replace the happiness that comes from having a loving child.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_271.context: Even Indra felt sad because of tears. No wealth can replace the joy of a son.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_272.meaning: Stories from the past teach us important lessons about life and how to treat others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_272.context: The speaker introduces a story about a talk between Indra and Surabhya the mother of cows.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_273.meaning: Kindness and mercy are powerful virtues that gods and humans should always practice in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_273.context: The sea cried out in pain. Indra showed mercy to Surabhya who is the mother of cows.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_274.meaning: When we see someone suffering we should ask why and try to understand their pain.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_274.context: Indra asks the beautiful Surabhya why she is crying so much about her situation today.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_275.meaning: A mother's love is so strong that she feels deep pain when her child suffers.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_275.context: Surabhya tells Indra she is crying for her son who is suffering greatly right now.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_276.meaning: Seeing our loved ones hurt causes us great sorrow and makes us want to help.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_276.context: She shows Indra her weak son who is being beaten by a farmer with a stick.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_342.meaning: Our own senses can be a greater danger than any outside foe we face.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_342.context: The five brothers face a hidden enemy that is faster than their deep sadness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_343.meaning: True strength and dignity remain visible even when you are in hiding or disguise.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_343.context: The brothers wear dark skins and stand tall like a mountain in the forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_344.meaning: Sudden fear can wake us up and change how we see the world around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_344.context: A dark woman appears and her fear makes the man open his eyes wide.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_345.meaning: Anger can make a person seem chaotic and dangerous, like a wild natural force.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_345.context: Dushasana looks wild and angry, like a river rushing between five high mountains.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_346.meaning: When our minds are scattered, we become easy targets for trouble or confusion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_346.context: The brothers catch the woman while she is confused and her senses are distracted.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_347.meaning: Wisdom and spiritual tools can help us defeat the scary illusions that try to hurt us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_347.context: A scary illusion rises up, and the wise man uses mantras to fight the demons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_348.meaning: When we lose control, our anger can make us look terrible and lose our true power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_348.context: The man loses his magic power and looks very angry with wide, fierce eyes.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_349.meaning: Facing the unknown with calm questions is better than reacting with fear or violence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_349.context: King Yudhisthira asks the dark figure to reveal who they are and what they want.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_386.meaning: Great strength can break through any obstacle, but violence often brings loud and scary destruction.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_386.context: Bhima fights a giant demon in a dark forest during a long and hard battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_387.meaning: True power comes from holding on firmly when the situation feels chaotic and unstable.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_387.context: The hero grabs the enemy tightly while the wind blows hard around them in the fight.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_388.meaning: Even the strongest people can get tired, and we must stay alert when others are weak.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_388.context: The tired enemy is held tight by the hero like a beast tied with a rope.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_390.meaning: Sometimes we must let go of our anger to find peace and rest after a struggle.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_390.context: Loud noises fill the air as the enemy loses consciousness from the heavy blows.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_391.meaning: Feeling joy when others suffer is wrong. We should show mercy instead of taking revenge.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_391.context: The hero feels happy seeing the enemy in pain, while others act on their wild desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_392.meaning: In a fight, you must protect yourself while trying to stop the other person from hurting you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_392.context: The hero strikes the enemy in the waist while the enemy tries to squeeze his neck.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_393.meaning: Death is the final end for everyone, and we must accept it without fear or sadness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_393.context: The hero tells the dying enemy to wipe his tears and go to the land of death.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_395.meaning: Anger can cloud our judgment, so we should stay calm and clear in our minds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_395.context: The hero looks at the enemy with anger while the enemy looks confused and scared.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_501.meaning: Even powerful people can feel fear and need help from wise guides when facing danger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_501.context: A group of famous men and their mothers fled, surrounded by top Brahmins, riding toward each other.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_502.meaning: Staying true to promises is important, even when traveling in difficult or unusual ways.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_502.context: They were not ministers; they rode a single wheel, the Pandavas kept their vows during travel.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_503.meaning: Danger can come from unexpected places, and we must be careful and brave when facing it.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_503.context: They met a strong demon goat, and people feared it because it ate humans.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_504.meaning: Using strength wisely helps protect others and move forward to new places.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_504.context: Bhima, the strongest fighter, killed the demon and went with his brothers to the city of Darupada.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_505.meaning: Celebrating others’ successes shows respect and encourages teamwork.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_505.context: Savyasachi found him there, and Krishna praised Rukmini, daughter of Bhishma, for her victory.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_506.meaning: Great achievements are rare and require effort, but they inspire others to try.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_506.context: Madhusoodana said he was defeated by Partha in a good fight, and others find it hard to do great deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_517.meaning: Strong words can stir emotions and remind us of the power of speech in important moments.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_517.context: Athaina spoke to Krishna in a brave gathering, saying the women’s horses would cry loudly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_518.meaning: Violence brings pain and loss, showing the need for peace and careful action.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_518.context: They were hit by many arrows, filled with blood, and many died on the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_476.meaning: Focus on present duties and urgent matters rather than dwelling on past stories or outdated traditions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_476.context: Arjuna asks Krishna to leave old tales and focus on the current crisis facing the Pandavas.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_477.meaning: Clever strategies can neutralize dangerous threats effectively, showing that wisdom often overcomes brute strength and power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_477.context: A story is told about a wolf tied up and thrown into the river by a clever person.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_478.meaning: Mental clarity and enlightenment empower you to take strong action and lead others with confidence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_478.context: Arjuna gains clarity and breaks free from confusion, allowing the mighty army of Bhima to rise.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_479.meaning: True safety comes from inner peace and divine protection, not just from avoiding external dangers.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_479.context: A man is shown sleeping among poisonous snakes, yet he remains safe and does not die.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_480.meaning: Righteous action may require difficult choices, balancing compassion with the need to stop evil forces.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_480.context: The Buddha figure strikes down snakes and kills a charioteer, showing a mix of mercy and violence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_481.meaning: Vulnerable lives are often at risk, reminding us to protect the innocent and care for the weak.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_481.context: Sleeping children are placed in a forest while a noble woman lies nearby, creating a tense scene.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_482.meaning: Fear is natural in hard times, but sharing burdens with friends helps you face challenges together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_482.context: Arya cries in fear while the Pandavas discuss their situation, surrounded by trouble and uncertainty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_483.meaning: Deep sorrow shows our love for family, but we must find peace even in the face of loss.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_483.context: A person laments their fate, fearing death and the loss of their children and grandchildren.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_907.meaning: Sharing your pain with trusted friends helps heal your heart and makes the burden of sorrow much lighter.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_907.context: Warriors rested in the woods after a long day and shared their deep feelings of sadness and loss together.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_908.meaning: True beauty comes from wisdom and purity of character, which guides leaders to make fair and just decisions for all.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_908.context: A beautiful and wise woman was present while a wise leader spoke important words to the king about duty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_909.meaning: Knowing you are innocent brings peace, but recognizing evil in others helps you stay strong and avoid their bad influence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_909.context: The speakers claimed they were innocent of any wrong doing while pointing out the cruel nature of their enemy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_910.meaning: Betraying family trust causes deep pain, so we must always communicate honestly and stand together with our loved ones.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_910.context: A king was exiled to the forest without telling his brothers, leaving them behind in a cruel and unfair act.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_911.meaning: A hardened heart leads to cruelty, so we must keep our hearts soft and kind to speak truth and love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_911.context: A person with a hard heart spoke harsh words against righteousness because of their own evil actions and bad choices.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_912.meaning: True happiness cannot come from hurting others, so we must seek joy that does not cause pain or suffering to anyone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_912.context: Evil people with their friends enjoyed happiness while causing suffering to others, showing a clear lack of moral justice.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_913.meaning: Simple living and humility bring true freedom, while ignoring our mistakes keeps us trapped in a cycle of guilt.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_913.context: Sinners did not cry for their wrongs while a king dressed in simple forest clothes prepared to leave the city.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1964.meaning: Sometimes we must hide our true self to survive danger and protect our peace from those who hurt us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1964.context: Nala hides his identity and acts foolish to avoid recognition by his enemies and former friends.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1965.meaning: True leaders inspire deep loyalty and concern from their people who care about their safety and well-being.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1965.context: Citizens and ministers gather at the palace gate because they are worried about their missing king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1966.meaning: A good ruler listens to complaints and acts with fairness to maintain order and protect the innocent.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1966.context: People report bad deeds to the king who values justice and duty above all other worldly things.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1968.meaning: Deep love brings intense pain when we see those we cherish suffering or losing their true identity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1968.context: Damayanti cries out in grief and shock when she realizes her husband has changed and is suffering.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1969.meaning: People naturally seek guidance and comfort from leaders they trust and respect during times of uncertainty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1969.context: The crowd begs the king to appear because they miss him and show their deep royal devotion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1970.meaning: Even strong people can be silenced by sorrow when life brings unexpected pain and heavy emotional burdens.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1970.context: The beautiful queen cries while the king remains silent and overwhelmed by the harsh forces of fate.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1971.meaning: Unmet expectations can lead to sadness but also remind us to keep hope alive for better times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1971.context: Ministers and citizens leave the palace area feeling sad and disappointed after failing to see the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1972.meaning: Patience and endurance are necessary when facing long periods of hardship and hiding from past mistakes.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_1972.context: Nala lives in disguise for many months while his brother Yudhisthira deals with the consequences.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2269.meaning: Focus on your path and trust that divine forces are watching over your journey through difficult times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2269.context: Nala counts steps while a snake speaks to him about his fate and the arrows he will face.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2271.meaning: Fear often disappears when you take action and move forward with courage in your daily life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2272.meaning: Face your fears directly because understanding the truth helps you accept your current situation with grace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2272.context: Nala stands shocked and disfigured as he sees the serpent revealing its true nature to him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2273.meaning: Sometimes hiding your identity protects you, allowing you to find peace and safety in difficult times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2273.context: The snake speaks kindly to Nala, explaining that it has hidden his true identity from others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2274.meaning: You must endure some pain and hardship before you can find freedom and relief from your troubles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2274.context: The snake warns that Nala must endure poison on his limbs before he can be released.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2275.meaning: Patience is required during suffering because your pain will eventually lead to a new beginning for you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2275.context: The warning repeats that Nala will stay in grief until his body is covered with poison.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2276.meaning: Your kindness and self control in hard times are noticed and rewarded by the universe around you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2276.context: The snake praises Nala for protecting it from anger and envy, showing his noble character.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2277.meaning: Trust that your past good deeds will protect you and bring success in your future challenges.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2277.context: The snake promises Nala will not suffer from poison and will win battles against his enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2357.meaning: Rekindling family bonds brings happiness; staying together strengthens love and support.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2358.meaning: Children need parental presence; absence can cause sadness and longing for family.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2358.context: A woman speaks about her daughters living far away, missing their father.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2359.meaning: Planning travel helps achieve goals; readiness and resources make journeys smoother.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2359.context: Someone wants to leave for Vidarbha, asking for a vehicle to travel quickly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2360.meaning: Respect and gratitude for generosity build strong relationships and community harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2360.context: A queen praises the king, noting their chariot filled with food and drink.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2362.meaning: Warm welcomes show acceptance; community support eases new beginnings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2362.context: She arrives in Vidarbha and relatives greet her warmly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2363.meaning: Togetherness creates joy; sharing moments strengthens bonds and well-being.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2363.context: Family members, daughters, and friends gather, all feeling well and happy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2364.meaning: Rituals unite people, honoring traditions and fostering spiritual connection.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2364.context: They worship gods, and a woman joins Brahmins in a sacred ritual.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2365.meaning: Generosity rewards loyalty; sharing wealth builds trust and respect among people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_2365.context: A king gifts a thousand cows to Sudeva, surrounded by his daughters and friends.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3309.meaning: Stay calm and trust your strength; fear will fade when you focus on your purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3309.context: Arjuna faces many enemies, his mind is full of worries and arrows of doubt.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3310.meaning: Believe in your own power and let others handle their problems without interference.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3310.context: A warrior says he is enough to protect everyone, and no one should fight his enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3312.meaning: Take action without letting fear or worry stop you from doing what is right.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3312.context: Arjuna is urged to fight, but the wise seer says he should not be burdened by fear.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3313.meaning: Seek places and people that support kindness and generosity, and share your blessings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3313.context: A forest saint talks about a place full of food, fruit, and good deeds.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3315.meaning: Patience and hope can bring relief; trust that help will arrive when needed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3315.context: They wait for Arjuna, hoping he will bring rain like a cloud after a long drought.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3316.meaning: Nature’s beauty reminds us of spiritual peace and the importance of caring for the earth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3316.context: Many holy places are known for lakes, rivers, and beautiful mountains.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3317.meaning: Support from friends can lift spirits and help you face challenges with confidence.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3317.context: The Pandavas feel sad, but a wise man comforts them with encouraging words.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3319.meaning: Learning about sacred places can inspire respect for nature and deepen spiritual understanding.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3319.context: A king is invited to visit a holy hermitage and learn about sacred mountains.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3459.meaning: Even in war, some places remain holy and protect people from danger.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3460.meaning: Faith and respect for the divine bring blessings and honor to leaders.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3460.context: We will get good rewards because of your help, you are the ruler of holy places and great kings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3462.meaning: Power and sacred visits help us cleanse our mistakes and find peace.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3462.context: They were saved by your strength and went to holy places, where we can wash away sins.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3463.meaning: True leadership combines strength, wisdom, and respect for tradition.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3464.meaning: Exploring spiritual realms can reveal hidden blessings and deeper understanding.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3464.context: The great king of India will find hidden worlds filled with sacred places.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3465.meaning: Nature and sacred sites inspire reverence and a desire for spiritual guidance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3465.context: We wish to see the king among holy mountains, rivers, and trees.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3466.meaning: Spiritual obstacles need courage and protection to overcome evil forces.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3466.context: Holy places can block hard work, but you should protect yourself from scattered demons.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3468.meaning: Listening to spiritual teachers helps us find and honor sacred places.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3468.context: Wise sages mention holy places, and great ascetics share their teachings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3605.meaning: Fear can make wise people lose their calm judgment and ability to think clearly during dangerous or scary situations.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3605.context: Royal advisors felt scared and confused when they saw the demon Vatapi standing before them in his true form.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3607.meaning: True strength comes from calm confidence and the willingness to face threats directly to protect others from harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3607.context: Sage Agastya told the frightened kings not to worry because he promised to eat the dangerous demon himself.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3608.meaning: Stay peaceful and grounded even when enemies try to intimidate you or laugh at your quiet confidence.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3609.meaning: Taking decisive action against evil can remove danger quickly and show that good power is stronger than evil.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3609.context: Agastya ate the entire demon Vatapi, defeating the threat completely and leaving the demon king shocked and silent.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3610.meaning: Witnessing the fall of a loved one brings deep sorrow and highlights the finality of defeat.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3610.context: A wind blew past Agastya, and the demon king Ilvala felt sad seeing his brother completely defeated.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3611.meaning: When plans fail, it is wise to pause and ask for advice before making your next move.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3611.context: Ilvala folded his hands and asked his ministers why they had come and what he should do now.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3612.meaning: Knowing your true worth and identity helps you stay humble and respectful even when facing strong opponents.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3612.context: Agastya laughed gently at Ilvala and reminded him that everyone knows his true identity as a powerful lord.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3613.meaning: It is better to seek fair solutions through peaceful negotiation rather than using force or causing harm to others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_3613.context: Agastya asked for a fair share of wealth without using violence, showing that peace is better than war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4652.meaning: Being chosen for a holy task shows that your skills and character are valued by the community.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4653.meaning: Asking for permission before acting shows deep respect for elders and family bonds in ancient times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4653.context: The brothers asked their father for permission to visit a hermitage where their father and mother lived.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4654.meaning: Sometimes we see things that look different from what they really are, leading to confusion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4654.context: One son went home and saw his father wearing a black deerskin while working in the forest.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4655.meaning: Mistakes made in a moment of fear or confusion can lead to tragic and irreversible consequences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4655.context: The son thought his father was a deer and killed him, then tried to save his own body.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4657.meaning: Even after a terrible mistake, we must face the reality and speak the truth to those we love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4657.context: The son performed funeral rites for his father, then his brother returned and spoke to him about the event.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4658.meaning: Sharing your burden with someone you trust helps you handle heavy guilt and painful truths better.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4658.context: The brother admitted he killed the deer because he mistook it for his father and could not carry the guilt alone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4659.meaning: Sometimes people believe their actions were justified by duty, even when they caused great harm to others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4659.context: The brother claimed he did the right thing for the Brahman and said he could handle the situation alone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4660.meaning: True devotion can lead people to make extreme sacrifices, but it also raises hard questions about right and wrong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4660.context: One brother offered to kill a Brahmin to help the other perform a sacrifice, keeping his senses under control.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4735.meaning: Deception and evil plans can harm others, but truth and courage can overcome them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4735.context: A villain uses magic tricks to try to kill a hero in a battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4736.meaning: Even those who seem powerful can be dangerous, so stay alert and trust good friends.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4736.context: An enemy who has turned against the hero is cruel and frightening.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_4737.meaning: Loss and danger can happen, but sharing good things brings joy to everyone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8099.meaning: Faith and good intentions can guide you through difficult times like a strong vehicle.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8099.context: A warrior changes his role to drive a chariot powered by faith and salvation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8100.meaning: When leaders are defeated, the group often loses its courage and starts to scatter.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8100.context: The divine warriors defeat the enemy charioteer, causing the whole army to run away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8101.meaning: Leaders must be present to guide their people, or the group will lose its direction.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8101.context: A leader turns the enemy army away, but Duryodhana is not there to help.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8286.meaning: Everyone should work together and help the king, showing loyalty and teamwork.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8286.context: Soldiers and people near kings are human. They should meet and fight for the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8287.meaning: We should be grateful for help, even if it seems accidental, and recognize good deeds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8287.context: The king asks if the Pandavas saved people by chance.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8288.meaning: Choosing the right companions matters; avoid bad influences and stay on a good path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8288.context: The king is told he should not live with the Pandavas and follow their army.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8289.meaning: Courage and punctuality show respect and dedication to duties and leaders.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8289.context: Brave warriors did not run away. They arrived at the king’s meeting early.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8290.meaning: Value what you have, stay calm, and trust that good things will happen.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8290.context: The king keeps his precious items. He sees the Pandavas in a good place.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8291.meaning: Celebrate wisely; avoid events that bring sorrow or trouble to your community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8291.context: The king wonders why people in his land regret celebrating the Pariyas.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8292.meaning: Commitment to a leader shows devotion, but true service requires the leader’s support.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8292.context: The speaker says he will stay if the king does not act, serving his feet.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8293.meaning: Stay close to those you respect, but avoid positions that make you look foolish.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8293.context: The speaker cannot live without the king, but warns against sitting opposite him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8510.meaning: Treating visitors with kindness helps you become a better person. It removes jealousy and builds a pure and humble spirit.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8510.context: A king shows great respect to guests, which helps him grow in politeness and remove envy from his heart.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8512.meaning: True value comes from a pure heart, not fancy things. Simple acts done with love bring great spiritual growth and joy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_8512.context: Sages live in simple homes, but their pure hearts and sacrifices make their simple food spiritually rich and abundant.
