hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9506.meaning: Showing respect to others brings inner peace and satisfaction with what life provides.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9506.context: Rama respectfully honors a woman and feels happy seeing the valuable gems she possesses.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9507.meaning: Completing your duties allows you to return home safely with trusted friends by your side.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9507.context: After allies leave, Rama returns to his city with Sugriva following him closely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9508.meaning: Guiding others through difficult times with kindness helps them find their way forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9508.context: Vibhishana and Sugriva follow Rama as they show the captive woman the forest path.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9510.meaning: When you finish your work, honor those who helped you by giving them their due respect.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9510.context: Rama arrives at the city and crowns Angada as king after finishing his tasks.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9511.meaning: Returning to your roots with family brings comfort and closes the journey properly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9511.context: Rama and Lakshmana travel back to their home city using the same road they came.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9512.meaning: Sharing important news quickly helps others understand what is happening around them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9512.context: A woman sees a sign and tells a man, while another traveler arrives at a village.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9514.meaning: True humility means staying simple and grounded even when you hold power or status.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_3_9514.context: A traveler sees a prince in rough clothes sitting on a simple chair.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1038.meaning: Bright, strong tools help you shine and protect others in daily life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1038.context: Sahadeva shows arrows shaped like the sun, symbolizing bright power.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1039.meaning: Wealth and power should be used wisely to help people and stay strong.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1039.context: The king wears yellow robes and carries golden arrows, showing wealth and strength.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1040.meaning: Be prepared and strong to face challenges and carry responsibilities.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1040.context: Arjuna’s arrow is long and sharp, ready for battle and heavy duty.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1041.meaning: Use your strength to protect others and keep enemies away.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1041.context: Bhimasena’s arrow is powerful like a tiger’s neck, frightening enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1042.meaning: True wisdom comes from inner strength, not from weapons or power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1042.context: Suphalash and Hematsarur are great weapons, but the wise king has no sword.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1043.meaning: Strong skills help you hold up heavy responsibilities and stay steady.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1043.context: Naluk has five nails in a treasury, showing strong, weight-bearing skill.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1044.meaning: Keep your tools pure and ready to help others whenever needed.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1044.context: A pure sword belongs to Sahadeva, ready to carry all burdens.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1045.meaning: Good tools and quick thinking help you succeed and impress others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1045.context: Great men’s weapons are gold-decorated, shining for quick-witted Parthians.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1445.meaning: True confidence comes from skill and preparation. A brave warrior stays calm and ready for any challenge.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1445.context: Arjuna laughed confidently while holding his famous bow during a fierce and intense battle scene.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1446.meaning: Face your fears with courage. Even when the enemy seems wild and strong, you must stand firm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1446.context: Arjuna faced his enemy who was powerful and wild like a drunk elephant leader in the fight.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1447.meaning: Great conflicts test our strength. We must stay focused and brave when facing powerful opposition in life.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1447.context: Two great heroes clashed on the ground in a fierce battle that shook the earth around them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1448.meaning: Witnessing great skill inspires us. We should respect dedication and the hard work of others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1448.context: The army watched in awe as two mighty warriors fought with incredible speed and power together.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1449.meaning: Actions have sharp consequences. Be careful with your words and deeds, as they can hurt others deeply.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1449.context: The warriors shot arrows that moved like deadly snakes, striking each other with great force and speed.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1450.meaning: Stay steady like a mountain. Inner strength and endless effort help you overcome any difficult obstacle.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1450.context: Arjuna had endless arrows and stood firm like a mountain, showing his strength and steady resolve.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1451.meaning: Skill beats speed alone. Practice makes perfect, and true mastery allows you to surpass your rivals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1451.context: Ashvatthama shot arrows quickly, but Arjuna proved to be even faster and more skilled in combat.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1452.meaning: Anger can be loud and destructive. Control your emotions so they do not lead you to ruin.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_4_1452.context: Karna drew his bow in great anger, creating a loud roaring sound that filled the battlefield.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_884.meaning: Life moves fast, and we must stay calm and ready for the challenges that come our way.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_884.context: A warrior describes his fast chariot ride and the enemy arrows waiting for him at dawn.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_887.meaning: We should always seek guidance from those who are truly wise and hold high moral standards.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_887.context: A speaker asks to hear wise words from a respected sage in a line of royal teachers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_902.meaning: A wise person speaks kindly to others and never uses harsh or insulting words in conversation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_902.context: The text describes how a true scholar praises others and avoids speaking badly of anyone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_903.meaning: True wisdom means understanding your feelings and not letting them stop you from seeing the truth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_903.context: The verse lists strong emotions like anger and joy as key parts of human respect and dignity.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_904.meaning: Real wisdom is shown by your actions, not just your words, even when no one is watching you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_904.context: A wise person performs secret actions that others cannot see, but their good deeds are known.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_905.meaning: A strong mind stays steady and calm, no matter what hard situations or bad feelings you face.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_905.context: The text says a wise person is not stopped by cold, heat, fear, or strong desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_906.meaning: You should do your best in everything and treat all people with respect and kindness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_906.context: The wise try to do their best and do not look down on any task or person.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_908.meaning: Use your knowledge and life to help others, not just for your own personal gain or desire.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_908.context: A wise person studies deeply, worships for the right reasons, and uses their life to help others.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1004.meaning: When we create problems, we also create chances for good outcomes if we plan well for tomorrow.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1004.context: A story about stirring up trouble and how good results come from desired future plans.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1005.meaning: Doing good work at the right time brings rewards, benefits, and new opportunities for growth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1005.context: A farmer who harvests fruit on time gets juice, seeds, and more fruit again.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1007.meaning: Treat each part of life gently; avoid harming foundations to keep beauty and life intact.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1007.context: Look for each flower carefully, don’t cut roots, like a garland, not a charcoal maker.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1009.meaning: True wisdom lasts forever, but even good actions can feel meaningless if not aligned with deeper purpose.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1009.context: Some truths are eternal, like a Buddha, and good deeds may still feel useless.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1012.meaning: Balancing what we see, think, say, and do, and sharing with others, brings happiness and harmony.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1012.context: Four aspects: sight, mind, speech, action; giving to the world brings joy.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1014.meaning: Fear can drive us away, but perseverance leads to safety, even if we feel isolated afterward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1014.context: Creatures flee from a hunter, and at sea’s end a lost traveler finds land and is left alone.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1015.meaning: Past achievements can feel fleeting; true legacy depends on lasting values, not just power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1015.context: Ancestors ruled proudly, but wind made their glory seem like a dream that moved elsewhere.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1016.meaning: Leading with honesty and fairness brings abundance and growth for everyone around.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1016.context: A king started righteous, and the earth became rich and prosperous.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1034.meaning: People who control their feelings walk the right path. You should avoid the wrong choices of bad people.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1034.context: The text compares two different life paths, one for wise people and one for bad people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1035.meaning: Virtue helps you win everything. Good character conquers all obstacles and proves your worth to others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1035.context: A great leader wins a battle and shows that good character beats lowly behavior.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1036.meaning: When you lose your core goodness, you lose interest in life. You stop valuing wealth or your loved ones.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1036.context: A person loses their main virtue and stops caring about life, money, or family.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1037.meaning: You can master your senses. You move from having nothing to being full of inner spiritual wealth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1037.context: The text describes how a person gains control over their senses and desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1039.meaning: Most people fear death. But truly noble people fear losing their dignity and honor even more.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1039.context: People fear death and bad endings, but noble people fear losing their honor most.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1041.meaning: You can master your senses. You move from having nothing to being full of inner spiritual wealth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1041.context: The text describes how a person gains control over their senses and desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1042.meaning: Most people fear death. But truly noble people fear losing their dignity and honor even more.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1042.context: People fear death and bad endings, but noble people fear losing their honor most.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1046.meaning: You can master your senses. You move from having nothing to being full of inner spiritual wealth.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_1046.context: The text describes how a person gains control over their senses and desires.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4315.meaning: True loyalty means standing firm in duty even when facing great hardship or suffering from your opponents.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4315.context: A warrior speaks of serving a holy woman and vows to fight back against enemies with great pain.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4316.meaning: Great respect and humility go together when you honor those who carry the weight of tradition and duty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4316.context: The speaker compares the honor of a warrior to the respect shown to a sacred symbol in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4317.meaning: Doing your duty correctly is more important than personal feelings or family ties in times of conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4317.context: A father declares he will fight a warrior better than his own son to uphold the code of honor.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4318.meaning: Recognize the unique power of others and understand that some skills are truly unmatched by anyone else.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4318.context: The speaker admits that no other archer in the world can match the skill of this terrible warrior.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4319.meaning: People who act with evil intent and deceit do not earn respect or worship from those who live virtuously.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4319.context: The text describes a person who is hostile, deceitful, and unrighteous, comparing them to a fool at a ceremony.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4320.meaning: Your inner nature drives your choices, so a good heart naturally seeks what is right and pure.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4320.context: The verse explains how sinful people desire sin even when warned, while good people desire good even when tempted.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4321.meaning: Be aware that harmful forces exist in the world and can cause damage if you are not careful.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4321.context: The speaker warns that myths and stories are present, and evils are meant to be harmful to the best people.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4322.meaning: Do not assume your power allows you to break rules or boundaries without facing serious consequences or resistance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_5_4322.context: The speaker challenges an opponent who thinks they can cross a boundary just because they believe they have strength.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_62.meaning: Nature reacts with fear and confusion when great violence and chaos happen around us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_62.context: Birds and insects make strange noises during the terrible war between cousins.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_63.meaning: Signs of destruction appear everywhere when people choose war instead of peace and love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_63.context: Warriors ride horses while swarms of locusts appear in the red rivers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_64.meaning: Extreme suffering and death can feel like a natural disaster for everyone involved.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_64.context: The sky glows red and blood and bones fall like heavy rain.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_65.meaning: No one is safe from the bad effects of widespread anger and conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_65.context: Even respected saints and kings are affected by the terrible events happening now.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_66.meaning: The universe itself seems to shake when moral order is broken by humans.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_66.context: Planets and stars seem to show fear and trouble in the sky.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_67.meaning: Even animals feel the deep sorrow and pain of human suffering and war.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_67.context: Thunder rumbles without clouds and the chariot horses cry tears of sadness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_68.meaning: When natural laws are broken, strange and confusing things happen in the world.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_68.context: Cows have donkey babies and trees bloom at the wrong time of year.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_69.meaning: Deep moral failure causes nature to become twisted and unnatural for all living beings.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_69.context: Women give birth to monsters and birds and deer act very strangely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1807.meaning: Even close allies can turn away, showing that loyalty may fail during war and hardship.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1807.context: Friends are ignored while Bhishma and Daruna are burning in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1809.meaning: Great power can overwhelm others, reminding us that strength must be used wisely and with care.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1809.context: Bhishma and Daruna use powerful weapons against many warriors.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1810.meaning: Strong teamwork can defeat enemies, but it also shows the danger of uncontrolled anger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1810.context: Krishna and Bhishma fight fiercely with many people around them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1811.meaning: Peaceful leaders can soothe even the fiercest warriors, teaching that calm can overcome conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1811.context: A great archer calms Bhishma, like clouds of fire.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1812.meaning: With divine help, good people can achieve victory and bring joy to their families.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1812.context: Govinda helps Pandavas defeat foes and win the kingdom.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1813.meaning: Thoughtful reflection can help us understand grief and find a way to move forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1813.context: Partha thinks deeply after speaking, feeling sorrow for a long time.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1814.meaning: Encouragement and courage can ease sorrow, showing that strength comes from unity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1814.context: A leader tells Bharatas not to grieve, praising brave brothers.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1816.meaning: Protecting elders and leaders shows respect and the importance of caring for those who guide us.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_1816.context: The king and Satyakisha guard the old Virata, Drupada, and Dhrishtadyumna.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3384.meaning: Their skill shows that bravery and expertise can protect many people during war.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3384.context: Chekitanas, Varshney, and Gautama were skilled charioteers fighting in a large army battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3385.meaning: Even strong warriors can be defeated by clever opponents, reminding us to stay alert.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3385.context: Marisha broke a bow, and his charioteer fell while Kashiprahasta killed the horse and charioteer.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3386.meaning: Consistent effort and teamwork help keep the enemy at bay during conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3386.context: Chekitanas, Varshney, and Gautama again defended the army with powerful arrows.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3387.meaning: Repeated attacks can break defenses, showing the importance of resilience.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3387.context: Marisha again broke a bow, and the charioteer was thrown down by Kashiprahasta.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3389.meaning: Quick action and courage can turn the tide in a dangerous situation.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3389.context: Satvata left his chariot, grabbed a club, and attacked Gautama’s horse and charioteer.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3390.meaning: Even when down, skillful use of weapons can still harm the enemy.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3390.context: Gautama on the ground fired sixteen arrows that pierced Satvata and struck the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3391.meaning: Anger can lead to violent plans, but wisdom is needed to choose better actions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3391.context: Chekitanas angrily threw a club; Purandara wanted to kill Gautama like Vritra.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3392.meaning: Combined force and many attacks can defeat a powerful opponent.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3392.context: A strong club struck her, and many arrows stopped Gautama.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3791.meaning: True power comes from moving with purpose and confidence, even when facing overwhelming odds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3791.context: A wolf warrior charges into battle with great speed, roaring loudly like a fierce lion.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3794.meaning: Honesty and skill go hand in hand, guiding leaders to protect their people with honor.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3794.context: A truthful warrior named Saucitti joins the fight, followed by skilled archers who lead the army.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3795.meaning: Strong teams are built by bringing together different talents and skills to face challenges together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3795.context: Several brave warriors and skilled charioteers gather together to support their side in the great war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3796.meaning: Unity and collective strength can surround and overcome even the most dangerous threats.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3796.context: A powerful lord arrives with his full strength, and they surround a demon with many chariots.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3797.meaning: Loyalty to a cause can inspire many people to stand together and defend what matters.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3797.context: Six thousand fierce warriors protect a demon king, showing their loyalty and readiness for battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3798.meaning: Chaos and noise often surround big events, but staying calm helps you see clearly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3798.context: The loud sounds of lions, chariots, and hooves make the ground shake during the intense fight.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3799.meaning: Fear is a natural reaction to danger, but recognizing it helps you find your courage.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3799.context: A warrior hears sounds of falling and feels shocked, while another becomes pale with fear.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3800.meaning: Conflict can be scary, but facing it with skill and bravery leads to resolution.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_3800.context: Skilled drivers shoot many different weapons at each other, creating a fierce and scary battle scene.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4511.meaning: True strength comes from within. When people act with courage, they shine like fire and wind.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4511.context: The poem compares two mighty warriors to natural forces and gods to show their power.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4512.meaning: Sometimes you must step up to help friends. Do not hide when duty calls you to act.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4512.context: A warrior asks a king to let him fight a famous enemy in the great war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4513.meaning: Confidence in your skills helps you face hard challenges. Trust yourself to do what is right.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4513.context: A brave hero promises to defeat a powerful enemy in front of everyone watching the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4514.meaning: Loyalty to truth can be hard. You may face difficult choices that test your deepest bonds.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4514.context: A grandson declares he will fight his own grandfather in a one on one chariot duel.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4515.meaning: Believe in your ability to overcome obstacles. Your inner power can help you win the day.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4515.context: A warrior compares his battle power to a god and promises to knock his enemy down.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4516.meaning: Real friendship means standing together. You share the joys and sorrows of the people you love.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4516.context: A friend declares that anyone who hurts his friend is also an enemy to him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4517.meaning: Sharing food builds strong bonds. Treating friends like family creates a deep sense of trust and care.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4517.context: A man calls his friend a relative and disciple, then talks about sharing food together.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4518.meaning: Sacrifice shows true love. Sometimes you must give up your own safety to keep others safe.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_6_4518.context: A warrior asks a king to fight him so he can protect his friend in the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_301.meaning: True strength creates fear in enemies. Your power and courage can stop others from attacking you directly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_301.context: Arjuna fights fiercely on the battlefield. His loud bow sounds scare the enemy troops greatly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_303.meaning: Great warriors face death often. Their bravery changes the outcome of battles and history forever.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_303.context: Arjuna defeats many warriors in the war. He sends many soldiers to their final resting place.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_305.meaning: Speed alone is not enough. You need powerful tools and loud presence to win against fast foes.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_305.context: The enemy horses run fast but cannot catch Arjuna. His bow roars like thunder clouds loudly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_306.meaning: Divine support makes you strong. With the right help, you can overcome any powerful enemy easily.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_306.context: Arjuna drives a divine chariot given by Vishvaksena. Even gods find it hard to defeat him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_307.meaning: Youth and skill go together. Being smart and brave helps you succeed in difficult challenges.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_307.context: The Pandava brothers are young and brave. They are smart and skilled in fighting battles.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_308.meaning: Stay calm when surrounded. Your courage can protect you even when many people attack you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_308.context: Nakula fights bravely against many Kaurava soldiers. He stands firm while surrounded by enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_309.meaning: Bravery draws attention. When you act with courage, others will notice and question your strength.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_309.context: Soldiers surround Nakula as he moves forward. They wonder who these brave fighters really are.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_311.meaning: Strength and beauty can coexist. A true hero is powerful in battle and graceful in appearance.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_311.context: A warrior defeats a large army from Sauvira. He is strong and beautiful in every way.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1377.meaning: True greatness comes from pure actions and smart choices. No one else has ever shown such perfect moral strength and character.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1377.context: A speaker praises a hero's unmatched virtue and wisdom during the great war, addressing Krishna directly with deep respect.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1378.meaning: Good character stands out above all else. This person shows us that true virtue is rare and worth admiring greatly.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1378.context: The narrator highlights the unique goodness of a warrior, comparing his deeds and fame to nothing else in history.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1379.meaning: We should seek to be like those who act with pure intent. Their example teaches us how to live well.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1379.context: Another verse repeats the praise for a hero's superior moral standing, emphasizing his unique place among all men.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1381.meaning: History remembers those who stand firm in duty. Their courage shows us the importance of facing challenges bravely.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1381.context: The text lists mighty warriors and kings who fought on the battlefield during the final days of the age.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1382.meaning: Excellence in action is rare. We should strive to do our best with skill and dedication in all tasks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1382.context: A speaker compares the fierce battle actions of a hero to past events, finding no equal to his skill.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1383.meaning: Kindness and humility make a person truly strong. Being gentle and controlled helps us build better relationships with others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1383.context: The verse describes a teacher who is kind, humble, and self-controlled, listing specific positive traits of noble characters.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1384.meaning: True strength includes both power and kindness. Being strong but gentle makes you a safe and reliable person.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1384.context: The text compares a hero's strength and sweetness to a mighty fortress, highlighting his balanced power and grace.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1385.meaning: Good traits can combine in one person. We should try to gather many virtues to become our best selves.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_1385.context: The narrator says that all the good qualities of Krishna and the Pandavas are found together in one young hero.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3709.meaning: When you face a challenge, prepare yourself fully and act with focused determination.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3709.context: A warrior gets ready for battle and chases his enemy with great eagerness.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3710.meaning: Fear can make strong groups hesitate, but courage helps you keep moving forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3710.context: Darkness follows the fleeing warrior, and the large white army becomes angry and stops.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3711.meaning: Even strong teams can feel discouraged when a single brave opponent blocks their path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3711.context: The Panchala army reaches their chariot but feels discouraged because a brave enemy stopped them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3712.meaning: When you are confused, you might use too many tools instead of finding the right one.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3712.context: Soldiers are confused and try to stop a fast chariot by shooting arrows around it.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3713.meaning: A good leader values fairness and seeks worthy opponents rather than easy victories.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3713.context: The narrator describes the mixed army and the best warriors seeking battle with honor.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3715.meaning: People respect those who are skilled and strong, and they often look up to them.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3715.context: The people praise a warrior named Paraudham for his strong skills and wonderful appearance.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3716.meaning: True strength comes from being balanced in body and mind, not just from power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3716.context: The text describes a person who is healthy, balanced, and has a long life.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3717.meaning: Having many skills and tools helps you handle different problems that come your way.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_3717.context: The warrior is equipped with many weapons and knows many ways to use them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4205.meaning: Together, people can move fast and create powerful change, showing teamwork and determination.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4205.context: A group sails quickly across a powerful ocean, stirring strong winds with their movements.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4206.meaning: Support from friends helps you win battles and keep moving forward toward your goals.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4206.context: A king is encouraged by Bhimasena and Panchalya, who kill enemies and continue their journey.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4207.meaning: Dreams of glory push people to act, but they must be ready for the consequences.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4207.context: The Tavakas pray for fame, decide to fight, and set out for battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4209.meaning: Protection and awareness help soldiers stay safe and ready for any danger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4209.context: Shields shine like the sun, and soldiers look around in many directions.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4211.meaning: Losses in war remind us that bravery can cost lives, and we must honor those who fall.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4211.context: A hero falls loudly, and many troops are lost in the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4213.meaning: Facing challenges bravely shows that leaders must stay committed, even when it is hard.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4213.context: Soldiers face hard times, and Duryodhana’s charioteer does not pull back from battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4214.meaning: One person can feel outmatched, but courage and skill can still make a difference.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4214.context: A single fighter meets many opponents in a great battle, feeling uneven against the king.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4215.meaning: True leadership attracts people with hope and generosity, creating a united and prosperous community.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_4215.context: A powerful lord brings happiness and wealth, and many follow without turning away.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5717.meaning: Shows how brave fighters use strong animals and vehicles to fight, highlighting power and teamwork.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5717.context: Warriors described as fierce like lions, riding elephants, chariots, and horses in a great battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5718.meaning: Illustrates danger in battle and the need for courage when facing strong opponents.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5718.context: A warrior’s head and neck were exposed while fighting with fierce followers and powerful enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5719.meaning: Shows that even in war, caring for family matters and staying calm is important.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5719.context: A hero fought demons who were angry and wanted to fight, while a mother worried about her son.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5720.meaning: Encourages trust, courage, and honesty to overcome fear and win battles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5720.context: A leader promised to defeat enemies, assured the army, and spoke truth to them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5722.meaning: Highlights the importance of leadership and the presence of many allies in a fight.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5722.context: After speaking to Ashvatthama, a warrior addressed Saubala, surrounded by many battle chariots.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5723.meaning: Shows respect for wisdom and devotion, encouraging people to value good thoughts.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5723.context: A speaker praised a great mind and devotion, calling someone a delight to Gautama.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5724.meaning: Reinforces the idea that strong support and many allies help in difficult battles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5724.context: Again, a warrior talked to Ashvatthama and Saubala, with many chariots around them.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5725.meaning: Encourages bravery, teamwork, and using great strength to achieve victory together.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_5725.context: With sixty thousand elephants, a leader urged Arjuna, Karna, Vrishasena, Kripa, and Nilasa to go beyond themselves.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7084.meaning: Keep your heart steady and do not let sadness or anger ruin your good judgment today.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7084.context: A wise elder tells Yudhisthira to stay calm and not let anger control his mind.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7085.meaning: Trust that your loved ones are safe and wait for the right time before acting in anger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7085.context: A spirit tells the king that his brothers are safe underground and warns him to stop fighting.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7087.meaning: Find deep joy in doing the right thing, because moral victory is the only real success.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7087.context: The old Pandavas leave after telling Yudhisthira that doing what is right is the true win.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7088.meaning: Losing a close family member in war brings intense sorrow and a strong urge to fight back.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7088.context: Yudhisthira feels deep pain and rage after seeing his brother Ghatotkacha die in the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7089.meaning: Sometimes you must step in to stop a situation from getting out of hand and causing harm.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7089.context: Dhrishtadyumna sees Bhima holding back a huge enemy army and tells him to stop the chaos.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7090.meaning: Use your inner strength boldly in hard times, and do not let fear stop you from acting.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7090.context: A warrior is told that his dark power comes from fire and he should fight without fear.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7091.meaning: Work together as a team to overcome a big challenge, and stay positive while you fight.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7091.context: Several warriors are told to attack the enemy from all sides with great joy and speed.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7092.meaning: Having loyal friends and family by your side makes you feel strong and ready for anything.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7092.context: Nakula and Sahadeva, along with their allies, are described as noble men who support the group.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7294.meaning: Strength and skill can overcome powerful opponents, showing that courage and physical power are vital in times of great conflict.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7294.context: Bhima fights fiercely in battle, knocking down the enemy charioteer and killing his companion with a heavy club.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7305.meaning: Using the right tools and skills with focus can help you overcome difficult challenges and achieve your goals effectively.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7305.context: Arjuna uses powerful divine weapons named after gods to strike his enemy, releasing arrows with great force and precision.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7306.meaning: When facing strong opposition, you must stay alert and ready to defend yourself against powerful and unexpected attacks.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7306.context: The Pandavas attack together, but their enemy responds by using supreme divine weapons against Arjuna in the fierce battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7307.meaning: Persistence and quick thinking allow you to neutralize threats, showing that steady effort can defeat repeated attempts to harm you.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7307.context: Arjuna repeatedly counters every weapon his enemy throws at him, blocking each attack to protect himself and win.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7308.meaning: Victory achieved through proper means brings peace of mind, reminding us that following rules leads to true success.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7308.context: The enemy is defeated by divine weapons following the rules of war, and Arjuna reflects on the battle mentally.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7309.meaning: Great moments make us feel connected to something larger, helping us see the bigger picture beyond our immediate struggles.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7309.context: The speaker feels a unique sense of power and presence, observing the armed men from all sides in the battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7310.meaning: Respecting limits and showing restraint can change the mood, proving that dignity and self-control are powerful traits.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7310.context: Arjuna stops his attack as forbidden, and the enemy smiles back at him amidst the crowd of great warriors.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7311.meaning: Important events attract attention from many sources, reminding us that our actions often have a wider impact than we realize.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7311.context: Gods, spirits, and sages appear in the sky to watch the battle, eager to see the outcome of the fight.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7860.meaning: Leaving safety to face danger shows great bravery but also highlights the extreme risk of fighting without proper defense.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7860.context: Soldiers leave their chariots to face a powerful weapon without any armor or protection on the battlefield.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7861.meaning: When enemies gain momentum and strength, it is important to stay calm and not let fear take over your mind.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7861.context: Warriors fight fiercely while their horses gain strength, making the opposing army seem more powerful and dangerous.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7862.meaning: Sometimes giving up the fight and surrendering is the only way to survive a situation that is too dangerous.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7862.context: Those who abandon their vehicles and drop their weapons will not be killed by this specific deadly weapon.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7863.meaning: Some forces are so overwhelming that resistance is futile, teaching us to recognize when a threat is unavoidable.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7863.context: Anyone who opposes this force will be destroyed, even those hiding deep underwater or trying to escape.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7864.meaning: True wisdom often leads people to change their actions and stop practices that are no longer right or helpful.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7864.context: The listeners hear wise words and decide in their hearts to abandon the current sacrifice or ritual completely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7865.meaning: Standing up for your values and refusing to give up your tools shows strong character and determination.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7865.context: Bhima sees the weapons and rejects the suggestion to throw them away, calling the advice unpleasant and wrong.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7866.meaning: Taking responsibility to protect others and stopping harm requires quick action and a strong sense of duty.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7866.context: Bhima declares that no one should release weapons here and promises to stop the enemy attack quickly.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7867.meaning: Confidence in your abilities is important, but comparing yourself to divine figures can show great pride or ego.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_7_7867.context: A warrior compares himself to Indra, the king of gods, claiming fame and strength in single combat.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2940.meaning: Even if you are strong, do not underestimate your opponents because they have great power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2940.context: A warrior warns Arjuna that the enemy forces are very strong and dangerous.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2941.meaning: True strength is needed to face the toughest challenges and overcome powerful enemies.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2941.context: A speaker praises Arjuna as the only one who can defeat the mighty king Bhagadatta.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2942.meaning: One person's dedication and skill can protect a whole group from harm and danger.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2942.context: The speaker tells Arjuna that his protection keeps the entire vast army safe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2943.meaning: Working together with strong allies helps you achieve goals that seem impossible alone.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2943.context: The text notes that Arjuna's support helped others defeat the great teachers Bhishma and Drona.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2944.meaning: Great skill and training make a person stand out and win against many others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2944.context: The speaker asks who can match the skill of the Panchala charioteers in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2945.meaning: Recognizing the strength of others helps you prepare better for any difficult situation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2946.meaning: Leadership requires strength and passion to guide a group through tough times.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_8_2947.meaning: Conflict brings great destruction, so it is wise to seek peace when possible.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_684.meaning: Seeing fierce conflict reminds us that power can be used for good or harm.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_685.meaning: Violence spreads everywhere, showing how war can overwhelm nature.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_686.meaning: Even in chaos, hidden truths can be seen if we look closely.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_687.meaning: Powerful actions can be beautiful yet dangerous, like bright but deadly light.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_688.meaning: Strong leaders inspire others to act bravely and unite for a common goal.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_688.context: Shalya, a fierce warrior, shows great skill; many brave fighters join him.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_689.meaning: War brings destruction, turning the earth into a battlefield of falling weapons.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_689.context: The king's weapons fly like birds; arrows and horses cover the ground.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_690.meaning: Past triumphs can guide present actions, showing the value of experience.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_690.context: Shalya's chariot moves in battle, reminding us of Indra's past victories.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_691.meaning: Desire for battle can equalize forces, teaching that passion fuels competition.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1275.meaning: Even the strongest fighters can fall, showing that no one is truly safe in battle.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1276.meaning: Great power can be destroyed quickly, reminding us that life is fragile and short.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1277.meaning: Trying to be like a hero can be dangerous if you are not ready for the risk.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1279.meaning: Grief can turn into rage, driving people to act without thinking or care for safety.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1280.meaning: Skill and powerful tools can be used for destruction, showing the danger of war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1281.meaning: In conflict, breaking an opponent's tools can stop them from fighting back effectively.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1282.meaning: Love for family can make a warrior pause, even in the middle of a deadly fight.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1282.context: Bhima takes a bow and calls out to his son, telling him to stay safe.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1283.meaning: War is a complex mix of terror and grandeur, leaving a deep mark on history.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_1283.context: The battle is described as huge, scary, and beautiful, like an old famous war.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2168.meaning: Sharing your pain with wise people can bring comfort and help you find a way forward.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2168.context: A woman shares her painful story with holy men who see her deep distress and fear.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2169.meaning: When you understand the root of a problem, you can work together to solve it effectively.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2169.context: The holy men listen to the cause of the curse and promise to help fix it.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2170.meaning: Working as a team allows us to overcome difficult challenges and help those in need.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2170.context: The sages agree to work together to free the river goddess from her heavy curse.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2171.meaning: Redemption is possible for everyone, and we can return to our true best selves.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2171.context: The river goddess is freed from her curse and shines brightly again as she did before.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2172.meaning: Admitting our weakness and asking for help is a brave step toward finding peace and relief.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2172.context: People admit they are suffering and poor, asking for help from the eternal father figure.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2174.meaning: Our careless actions create chaos, so we must act with care to keep life balanced.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2174.context: Negligence and bad deeds cause imbalance in the world, affecting both gods and demons equally.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2175.meaning: Respecting those who guide us builds a strong community and keeps our own hearts pure.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2177.meaning: Kind words and praise can heal wounds and guide even the lost toward a better path.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2177.context: The sages praise the river and speak kindly to demons to help them find salvation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2262.meaning: It reminds us that many things are seen as eternal, but true worth comes from inner devotion.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2262.context: The verse talks about idols, rivers, sacred books, holy places, and the earth.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2263.meaning: It shows how different divine aspects are connected, teaching unity in diversity.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2263.context: It names Aditi as mother, Hari as body, Saraswati as river, and lists other divine wives.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2264.meaning: It illustrates the power of nature and animals, encouraging respect for all living things.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2266.meaning: It highlights the balance between life, duty, and the inevitable end of all beings.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2267.meaning: It teaches that many paths exist, yet all lead to a common purpose or celebration.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2267.context: It says many gods are not listed because of their many forms, and they gathered for a coronation.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2268.meaning: It shows that sharing gifts with others strengthens community and faith.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2268.context: The king receives offerings from the gods, including vessels for rituals.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2269.meaning: It reminds us that true blessings come from pure sources and sincere intentions.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2269.context: The verse says the king filled golden urns with divine tools and holy river waters.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2270.meaning: It teaches that faith and support can empower a person to protect and lead others.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2270.context: The gods rejoice and consecrate a young boy who becomes a great army leader.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2407.meaning: Divine help gives courage to those who fight for justice and protects them from their enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2409.meaning: Preparation and unity make a group strong and impressive, showing readiness to face any challenge ahead.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2409.context: A huge army stands ready for battle, shining brightly with flags and weapons in the light.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2413.meaning: Victory in battle brings honor, and seeking divine approval shows respect for higher spiritual powers.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2413.context: The gods are asked to accept blessings from a warrior who has defeated many foes in combat.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2414.meaning: Support from others gives confidence, and a clear promise helps one overcome fear in difficult times.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2414.context: The army surrounds a warrior and grants him a wish, promising he will defeat his enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2415.meaning: Repeatedly seeking divine favor shows humility, reminding us that true strength comes from spiritual connection.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2415.context: The gods are again asked to accept blessings from a warrior who has killed many enemies.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2416.meaning: Fulfilling promises brings joy to others, and keeping your word creates lasting peace and happiness.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2416.context: Spirits of the dead cheer loudly because their wishes were granted by a powerful warrior.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2417.meaning: Success depends on good character traits like patience and honesty, not just physical strength or power.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2417.context: The army marches forward with virtues like patience, memory, and righteousness guiding their every step.

hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2419.meaning: Confidence and boldness are needed in tough times, but they must be used with purpose and control.
hinduism_mahabharata_book_9_2419.context: A fierce warrior holds weapons and roars like a lion, showing his power and readiness to fight.
